newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee economy starting to slow, report says.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee economy starting to slow, report says.

text.p: For the first time in years, Tennessee lags the U.S. average in certain economic growth categories, according to a quarterly report from the University of Tennessee's Center for Business and Economic Research.

The state's growth in per capita personal income ranked 47th among states in 1996. Tennessee personal income grew only 4.7 percent in 1996, compared to almost 7 percent growth in the previous two years. For the first quarter of 1997, personal income grew only 1.1 percent.
Tennessee also lagged in employment. The state's 5 percent unemployment rate exceeded the national average of 4.9 percent.
"It would appear that Tennessee has simply reached its full employment potential during the current economic expansion," the report said.
The study did not suggest a single explanation for the slowdown. But it said 15,000 non-durable goods manufacturing jobs had been lost, or about 6 percent of all jobs in the state.
The manufacture of cars, appliances and other durable goods slipped by a half percentage point in 1996. The deceleration follows 4.5 percent growth in 1994 and 2.2 percent growth in 1995.
Growth in construction and services jobs has been cut by half, the report said.

Economist Matt Murray, lead author of the study, said the state was one of the first to rebound from the recession in 1990 and may have reached a state of full employment that other states have not yet experienced.
